main_body: two-story tavern/house with pitched orange-brown tile roof and plaster/timber walls
top_band: orange-brown tiled roof slope with ridge cap and chimney opening from row 0 to row 44
evidence: The pitched roof acts as the top surface (rows 0-44, 45 rows tall) with a clear ridge cap (rows 0-2), chimney with visible top opening (rows 8-10), front eave edge at row 44, and eave shadow cast onto the upper plaster wall at rows 45-47. Below it sits the two-story south wall face (rows 45-95, 51 rows tall) with recessed doorway and window frames.

style.evidence: The candidate matches the Beodeul reference buildings in craftsmanship: rich 6-step shading on the orange-brown roof tiles with individual tile highlights, speckled plaster texture across the walls, wood-grain planks on the door and porch awning, stone base blocks, and selective dark-brown/dark-grey material-toned outlines.
